heartNotes: Gochujang is very salty, so this uses half as much and adds heat with salt-free gochugaru. The sea salt is left out, the homemade or low-sodium soy sauce cuts more sodium, and avocado oil replaces olive oil and is cut in half. Whole-wheat fettuccine adds fiber, and unsweetened almond milk keeps it creamy with no saturated fat.

title: Salt-Free Ranch Dry Mix
summary: One jar of salt-free ranch mix that makes creamy dressing, a thick dip, or a quick stand-in for canned cream-of soup.
replaces: Ranch seasoning packets and canned cream-of soups
ingredients: Creamy soup or sauce base (replaces 1 can of condensed cream-of soup):
1 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken, vegetable or beef broth
steps: Whisk all the mix ingredients together in a bowl until the powders are evenly blended and there are no lumps. Store in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place for up to 3 months. Shake or stir before each use.
Dressing: whisk 2 tablespoons of the mix with the yogurt, milk and lemon juice. Add milk a splash at a time to reach the thickness you like. Chill at least 30 minutes so the herbs soften.
Dip: stir 2 tablespoons of the mix into the yogurt and chill at least 30 minutes. Serve with raw vegetables.

Soup or sauce base: whisk 1/3 cup of the mix into the cold broth in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly, and cook 2 to 3 minutes until thick. Use it in casseroles anywhere a recipe calls for a can of condensed cream-of soup.
For a cream-of soup, stir 1/2 cup cooked mushrooms, broccoli, celery, potato or chicken into the thickened base and heat through.
notes: 2 tablespoons of mix replaces one store-bought ranch packet. The cornstarch only thickens when heated, so it won't change a cold dressing or dip. Buttermilk powder is in the baking aisle or near the powdered milk. Inspired by a homemade ranch seasoning from My Baking Addiction and a cream soup mix from thisoldbaker shared on Facebook.
heartNotes: There is no added salt. A ranch packet carries about 1,500 mg of sodium, and a can of condensed cream-of soup runs close to 2,000 mg. Here, extra garlic, onion, herbs, mustard and lemon carry the flavor instead. Nonfat buttermilk and milk powders keep it creamy with almost no fat, and nonfat Greek yogurt replaces the mayonnaise and sour cream in dressing and dip. The sugar is gone too. Buttermilk powder has a little natural sodium, so the mix is low-sodium rather than sodium-free.

title: Chickpea and Sweet Pea Salad with Dill and Lemon
summary: A bright, fiber-packed salad of chickpeas, sweet peas and red onion in a lemony dill dressing.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can low-sodium chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 cup sweet peas, fresh or frozen and thawed
1 teaspoon Homemade Whole-Grain Honey Mustard (from this site) or Dijon mustard
steps: Put the chickpeas, peas, red onion and dill in a large bowl.
Whisk the lemon zest, lemon juice, avocado oil, mustard, honey, garlic powder and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently.
Let it sit at least 10 minutes so the flavors blend. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, so it's an easy lunch to make ahead. Frozen peas only need a quick thaw under cold water. Inspired by a chickpea salad recipe shared on Facebook.
heartNotes: The salt is gone, and lemon zest, mustard and garlic carry the flavor instead. Low-sodium chickpeas replace regular canned, and there are more of them for extra protein and fiber. Avocado oil replaces the olive oil and is cut in half.

title: Crunchy Chickpea and Edamame Sesame Salad
summary: Crisp cabbage, carrots, chickpeas and edamame tossed in a ginger-sesame dressing, sturdy enough to pack for lunch.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can low-sodium chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 cup shelled edamame, thawed if frozen
1 tablespoon Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or low-sodium soy sauce
steps: Put the chickpeas, edamame, both cabbages, carrots and green onions in a large bowl.
Whisk all the dressing ingredients in a small bowl until well blended.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss well to coat.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and toss again.
Let it sit 10 to 15 minutes before serving. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
notes: A bag of coleslaw mix can stand in for the cabbages and carrots. Inspired by a chickpea and edamame salad recipe shared on Facebook.
heartNotes: Three tablespoons of sesame oil become 1 tablespoon of avocado oil plus 2 teaspoons of toasted sesame oil, which keeps the nutty flavor with about half the fat. The homemade or low-sodium soy sauce and low-sodium chickpeas cut the sodium, and a squeeze of lime adds brightness without salt.

title: Carrot Gnocchi with Sage
summary: Soft, sweet carrot gnocchi pan-crisped with fresh sage and a little Parmesan.
ingredients: 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 cup (125 g) all-purpose or tipo 00 flour, plus more for rolling
For the sage sauce (for half the batch):
steps: Steam or boil the carrots 15 to 25 minutes, until fork-tender. Drain completely and pat dry with a towel, removing as much moisture as you can.
Mash, rice or blend the carrots smooth. Let the steam escape until the puree is just warm, not hot.
Mix the carrot puree, egg yolk, nutmeg and both flours with a fork, then with your hands. Knead gently just until the dough comes together. It should be a little sticky; don't add extra flour.
Cover and rest the dough 10 to 30 minutes.
Cut the dough into 16 pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each into a rope about 1/2 inch thick and cut into 1/2-inch pieces.
Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a gentle boil. Cook the gnocchi in batches until they float, 2 to 3 minutes, then wait 30 seconds more and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
For the sauce, heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sage and garlic and cook until the sage is crisp, about 1 minute.
Add half the gnocchi and cook 5 to 8 minutes, turning, until lightly crisp. Season with the pepper and top with the Parmesan and lemon zest.
notes: To freeze the other half, spread uncooked gnocchi on a floured sheet pan, freeze until firm, then bag. Cook from frozen in simmering water. They're also good with the Red Sauce or Mushroom Sauce from this site. Inspired by a carrot gnocchi recipe shared by Crowded Kitchen on Facebook.
heartNotes: Avocado oil replaces 3 tablespoons of browned butter, which cuts most of the saturated fat. The kosher salt is gone from the dough and the cooking water, and nutmeg, sage, garlic and lemon zest carry the flavor instead. Half the flour is whole wheat for more fiber, and the Parmesan is kept to a tablespoon.

title: Brothy Parmesan Spaghettio Soup
summary: A nostalgic, brothy tomato soup with little pasta rings, simmered with a Parmesan rind for savory depth.
ingredients: 4 to 6 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
5 oz whole-wheat anelli or other small pasta rings
steps: Heat the avocado oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, red pepper flakes, oregano, basil and black pepper and cook 2 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens a little.
Add 4 cups of the broth and the Parmesan rind. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, about 8 to 10 minutes. Add up to 2 more cups of broth if you want it brothier.
Remove the rind. Stir in the lemon juice and serve.
notes: Save Parmesan rinds in the freezer for soups like this one; a small piece goes a long way. Regular anelli or ditalini works if you can't find whole wheat. Inspired by a recipe shared by britacooks on Facebook.
heartNotes: The butter is gone and avocado oil replaces the olive oil, cut to one tablespoon, so there's far less saturated fat. The teaspoon of salt is left out, and low-sodium broth and tomato paste replace the regular ones. A smaller Parmesan rind still gives the soup its savory flavor with much less sodium, and whole-wheat pasta adds fiber.

title: Salt-Free Cream of Anything Soup Mix
summary: A pantry jar that makes a quick, creamy base for casseroles and holiday cooking: cream of mushroom, chicken, celery, broccoli or cheddar.
ingredients: 1 cup nonfat milk, water or low-sodium broth
1/2 cup finely chopped cooked chicken breast
steps: Whisk all the mix ingredients together until evenly blended. Store in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months.
To use, whisk 1/3 cup of the mix into 1 cup of cold milk, water or broth in a small saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, 3 to 5 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Stir in an add-in and heat through. Use it anywhere a recipe calls for one 10.5-ounce can of condensed cream-of soup.
notes: Use low-sodium beef broth for cream of mushroom and low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth for the rest. Nutritional yeast is in the baking or health food aisle. For a ranch-flavored version, use the Salt-Free Ranch Dry Mix from this site. Inspired by cream soup mixes shared by the.homemade.fam and thisoldbaker on Facebook.
heartNotes: The original uses 1/2 cup of chicken bouillon powder, which is mostly salt. Nutritional yeast, onion, garlic, celery seed and herbs give the savory flavor with no added salt. A can of condensed cream-of soup carries close to 2,000 mg of sodium, and nonfat dry milk keeps this version creamy with almost no fat. Reduced-fat cheddar and a smaller amount keep the cheese version lighter.

title: Spicy Korean Cucumber Salad
summary: Crunchy cucumbers and bean sprouts in a tangy, spicy sesame dressing. Ready in 10 minutes.
ingredients: 1 English cucumber, or 3 small Persian cucumbers
2 teaspoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or low-sodium soy sauce
1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine (drinking-grade, not salted cooking wine)
2 to 4 teaspoons gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
Optional: sliced green onion and toasted sesame seeds, for topping
steps: Slice the cucumber in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Cut each half lengthwise again, then dice into small chunks.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Blanch the bean sprouts for 2 minutes, then move them straight into a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Drain well.
In a bowl, combine the cucumber, bean sprouts, soy sauce, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, black vinegar and gochugaru. Stir to combine.
Top with green onion and sesame seeds for some extra razzle dazzle, and serve.
notes: Start with 2 teaspoons of gochugaru and work up to 4 if you like the heat. It's best eaten the day it's made, before the cucumbers soften.
heartNotes: The homemade or low-sodium soy sauce keeps the sodium low, and there's no added salt. A single teaspoon of sesame oil is enough for flavor; the black vinegar and gochugaru do the heavy lifting. Use drinking-grade Shaoxing wine, since the cooking versions have added salt.
imageAlt: Spicy Korean cucumber salad with bean sprouts and gochugaru in a small bowl

title: Air Fryer Salmon
summary: Crispy-edged, tender salmon in 10 minutes with almost no prep. Season it however you like.
ingredients: Potassium chloride salt substitute, to taste (optional; see note)
Optional: your favorite salt-free seasoning or spice blend
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 400°F.
Pat the salmon dry. Season the flesh side with a light sprinkle of salt substitute, the black pepper and any other salt-free seasoning you like.
Place the fillets skin side down in the basket and air fry at 400°F for 5 minutes.
Flip the fillets and peel off the skin as you flip; it should come right off. Air fry 5 more minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F inside.
notes: Thicker fillets may need a minute or two more. Peeling the skin at the flip lets both sides brown. Great with lemon wedges and a side of the Spicy Korean Cucumber Salad. Potassium chloride salt substitutes aren't safe for everyone: if you have kidney problems or take certain blood pressure or heart medications, check with your doctor first, or skip it and use a salt-free blend.
heartNotes: Salmon is one of the best sources of heart-healthy omega-3 fats. The air fryer cooks it with no added oil, and potassium chloride gives a salty taste without the sodium.

title: Air Fryer Shrimp Fajitas
summary: Sizzling shrimp, peppers and onion straight from frozen in about 15 minutes, all cooked together in the air fryer.
ingredients: 1 lb frozen raw shrimp (tail-on is fine)
1 or 2 jalapeños, sliced (seeded for less heat)
2 tablespoons No-Salt Taco and Fajita Seasoning (from this site), divided
For topping: fat-free sour cream and shredded reduced-fat cheese
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 400°F.
Toss the onion, peppers and jalapeños with 1 tablespoon of the avocado oil and 1 tablespoon of the seasoning.
Put the vegetables on one side of the air fryer basket and the frozen shrimp on the other side. Air fry at 400°F for 15 minutes.

Halfway through, take out the shrimp and pull off the tails. Toss the shrimp with the remaining 1/2 tablespoon avocado oil and 1 tablespoon seasoning, then put them back in for the rest of the cooking time.
When the time is up, combine the shrimp and vegetables. Roll into warm tortillas and top with a spoonful of fat-free sour cream and a sprinkle of reduced-fat cheese.
notes: No need to thaw the shrimp; starting from frozen keeps them from overcooking. If your air fryer is small, cook in two batches. Warm the tortillas in the air fryer for the last minute.
heartNotes: Shrimp is lean protein, the salt-free seasoning replaces store-bought packets loaded with sodium, and a little avocado oil goes a long way. Fat-free sour cream, reduced-fat cheese and whole-wheat tortillas keep the toppings in check.

title: Lighter Shrimp or Chicken Alfredo
summary: Creamy garlic-Parmesan Alfredo with shrimp or chicken, made lighter with milk instead of heavy cream and a lot less butter.
ingredients: 8 oz fettuccine (whole wheat for extra fiber)
1 lb peeled shrimp, or boneless skinless chicken breast cut into bite-size pieces
Seasoning for the protein: black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and paprika, or a salt-free Cajun blend or salt-free togarashi
1 shallot, finely diced (or 1/2 small white onion)
3 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 spoonful jarred minced garlic)
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pot of unsalted water until al dente. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, season the shrimp or chicken. Heat the butter and avocado oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat and cook the protein through. Shrimp only takes 2 to 3 minutes; chicken takes 6 to 8. Move it to a plate.
Add the shallot to the pan and cook until soft, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth.
Simmer, stirring often, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon, 3 to 5 minutes. Season with the black pepper and red pepper flakes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Parmesan until melted and smooth.
Add the protein and pasta back to the pan and toss well. Add splashes of the saved pasta water to thin the sauce until the pasta is well coated. Top with parsley and serve.
notes: The flour does the thickening that reducing heavy cream does in a classic Alfredo, so the sauce stays creamy without the cream. For a special occasion, you can swap half the milk for half-and-half. Parmesan is naturally salty, so the sauce doesn't need any added salt. Want it spicy? Try the Spicy Gochujang Shrimp or Chicken Alfredo. Tortellini works great in place of the pasta too; store-bought filled pasta can be higher in sodium, so check labels.
heartNotes: A classic Alfredo uses heavy cream, a lot of butter and up to a cup of cheese. This version uses 1% milk thickened with a little flour, a tablespoon of butter plus a tablespoon of avocado oil, and 1/3 cup Parmesan, cutting most of the saturated fat. There's no added salt, the seasonings are salt-free, and whole-wheat pasta adds fiber.
imageAlt: Shrimp in a creamy Parmesan Alfredo sauce over tri-color cheese tortellini
imageCaption: Pictured with shrimp over prepackaged tortellini instead of pasta.

title: Spicy Gochujang Shrimp or Chicken Alfredo
summary: The lighter Alfredo with a kick: a tablespoon of gochujang turns the creamy Parmesan sauce sweet, smoky and spicy, finished with green onions.
ingredients: 8 oz fettuccine (whole wheat for extra fiber)
1 lb peeled shrimp, or boneless skinless chicken breast cut into bite-size pieces
Seasoning for the protein: black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and paprika, or salt-free togarashi
1 shallot, finely diced (or 1/2 small white onion)
3 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 spoonful jarred minced garlic)
Optional: 1/4 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, for extra heat
2 green onions, thinly sliced, for topping
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pot of unsalted water until al dente. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, season the shrimp or chicken. Heat the butter and avocado oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat and cook the protein through. Shrimp only takes 2 to 3 minutes; chicken takes 6 to 8. Move it to a plate.
Add the shallot to the pan and cook until soft, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth.
Simmer, stirring often, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon, 3 to 5 minutes. Whisk in the gochujang until fully blended, then season with the black pepper and red pepper flakes if using.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Parmesan until melted and smooth.
Add the protein and pasta back to the pan and toss well. Add splashes of the saved pasta water to thin the sauce until the pasta is well coated. Top with the green onions and serve.
notes: Gochujang brands vary in heat, so start with a tablespoon and taste before adding the red pepper flakes. Whisk it in after the sauce thickens so it blends smoothly. For the classic version, see Lighter Shrimp or Chicken Alfredo.
heartNotes: Same lighter base as the classic: 1% milk thickened with a little flour, a tablespoon each of butter and avocado oil, 1/3 cup Parmesan and no added salt. Gochujang does carry some sodium, so this sticks to one tablespoon for the whole pan, and the heat means you won't miss the salt.

title: Thai Chicken Meatballs in Coconut Red Curry
summary: Tender ginger-garlic chicken meatballs simmered with red peppers in a creamy coconut red curry with fresh basil and lime.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or low-sodium soy sauce
To serve: lime wedges, extra sliced green onion, and brown jasmine rice or rice noodles
steps: Mix the meatball ingredients (everything except the oil) gently until just combined; overmixing makes them tough. With damp hands, shape into 18 to 20 meatballs.
Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, 2 to 3 minutes, turning to color a few sides. They don't need to cook through. Move them to a plate.
In the same skillet, cook the onion until soft, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry paste and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the coconut milk, broth, fish sauce, soy sauce and honey until the curry paste is blended. Add the bell pepper and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return the meatballs to the pan. Cover and simmer gently 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through (165°F inside).
Stir in the lime juice and basil and let the basil wilt for a minute. Top with green onion and serve with lime wedges over brown jasmine rice or rice noodles.
notes: Curry pastes vary a lot in heat and salt; check the label and pick a lower-sodium brand if you can. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge and reheat well. Inspired by a recipe shared by Recipes Smart on Facebook.
heartNotes: The added salt is gone. The 2 tablespoons of fish sauce in the original become 1 teaspoon, the soy sauce is homemade or low-sodium, the broth is low-sodium, and there's a little less curry paste, which together cut most of the sodium. Light coconut milk replaces full-fat to cut saturated fat, avocado oil replaces vegetable oil and is used only for browning, honey replaces brown sugar, and lean chicken breast and whole-wheat panko keep the meatballs light.

title: Slow Cooker Mexican Chicken and Rice
summary: Chicken, brown rice, black beans, corn and tomatoes with green chiles cooked together in the slow cooker, then shredded and topped with melty cheese.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 oz) can low-sodium corn, drained (or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn)
1 (10 oz) can low-sodium diced tomatoes with green chiles
2 tablespoons No-Salt Taco and Fajita Seasoning (from this site)
For topping: sliced green onions and lime wedges
steps: Arrange the chicken in the bottom of the slow cooker.
In a bowl, stir together the rice, black beans, corn, tomatoes with their juice, taco seasoning, broth and pepper. Pour it over the chicken.
Cover and cook on low 6 to 7 hours or on high 3 to 4 hours, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F) and the rice is tender. If the rice looks dry near the end, stir in a splash more broth.
Shred the chicken right in the slow cooker with two forks and stir it into the rice and beans.
Sprinkle with the cheese, cover and let sit 10 minutes to melt. Top with green onions and serve with lime wedges.
notes: Great as burrito bowls, in whole-wheat tortillas, or over greens. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge. Inspired by a slow cooker recipe shared on Facebook.
heartNotes: A taco seasoning packet can carry well over 1,500 mg of sodium; the salt-free homemade blend replaces it, and the added salt is gone. Low-sodium beans, corn, tomatoes and broth cut the sodium further. Brown rice adds fiber, the beans add more, and a half cup of reduced-fat cheddar replaces a full cup of regular.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Lime Shredded Chicken
summary: Sweet, tangy shredded chicken with honey, lime and smoked paprika, made for tacos, salads and bowls with almost no effort.
ingredients: For serving: lime wedges and sliced green onions
steps: Put the chicken in the slow cooker.
Whisk the honey, lime juice and zest, garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, pepper and broth in a small bowl. Pour it over the chicken.
Cover and cook on low 6 to 7 hours or on high 3 to 4 hours, until the chicken is tender and cooked through (165°F).
Take the chicken out and shred it with two forks. Return it to the slow cooker and stir to coat it in the sauce.
Serve over brown rice, in whole-wheat tortillas or on a salad, with lime wedges and green onions.
notes: Freezes well in its sauce for up to 3 months, so it's an easy meal-prep protein. Inspired by a recipe shared by Foodie Idea on Facebook.
heartNotes: The salt is gone; lime zest, garlic, cumin, chili powder and smoked paprika carry the flavor. The honey is cut in half to 1/4 cup, which keeps the sweet-tangy glaze with much less added sugar. Skinless chicken breast keeps it lean, and the broth is low-sodium.

title: 15-Minute Saucy Dan Dan Noodles
summary: Linguine and crumbled lean pork tossed in a creamy, nutty tahini-chili sauce, topped with peanuts, scallions and sesame. Faster than takeout.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or low-sodium soy sauce
2 teaspoons chili crisp, plus 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (more or less to taste)
1 lb extra-lean ground pork (96% lean) or lean ground turkey
1 bunch green onions, finely chopped (save some for topping)
1 tablespoon cornstarch whisked with 3 tablespoons water
steps: Cook the linguine in a large pot of unsalted water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Whisk the sauce ingredients in a small bowl until smooth. In another small bowl, whisk the cornstarch and water into a slurry.
Heat the avocado oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the pork and break it into small crumbles as it cooks. When it's almost cooked through, add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and stir to coat the meat. Add most of the green onions and the slurry and stir for about a minute, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Add the noodles and toss until well coated. Top with the peanuts, the rest of the green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Not an authentic dan dan, but a fast weeknight take on it. Want more heat? Add red pepper flakes, not more chili crisp, which is salty. Inspired by a recipe shared by Kalejunkie on Facebook.
heartNotes: Extra-lean pork or turkey replaces regular ground pork, cutting a lot of saturated fat. The pasta water isn't salted, the soy sauce is homemade or low-sodium, and the chili crisp is cut from 2 tablespoons plus extra for topping to 2 teaspoons, with red pepper flakes adding the heat. The sesame oil is halved, the tahini trimmed, honey replaces maple syrup, the peanuts are unsalted and halved, and whole-wheat linguine adds fiber.
